subject: Post-demo recap: procurement readiness & hosting preference (PO vs Card)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olive-systems.com>; Emily Tan <emily.tan@olive-systems.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: procurement readiness & hosting preference (PO vs Card)

Hi Samir / Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion with the infra and procurement teams. Quick recap + actions so we have alignment on the commercial path before you kick off procurement: 

1) Hosting preference: you said the default is hosted API for proofs-of-concept, with Dedicated or Private considered for regulated workloads (PHI). Please confirm if the initial pilot must be in our hosted environment or if you want a Dedicated eval.

2) Payment flow: procurement indicated the preference is PO for enterprise purchases. Card is fine for early pilot spend under $5k/mo. Confirm whether the PO route is required for the pilot or only for Phase 2.

3) Commits vs On-demand: we covered a 6–12 month committed option (discounted unit price) vs on-demand. If procurement needs committed spend to justify Dedicated, let us know target commit level (GPU hours or $/month).

4) Security/compliance: Emily asked for audit logs, SOC2 evidence, and KMS integration notes — attaching a short playbook that answers those items.

Next steps (proposed):
- You confirm preferred hosting for the pilot (hosted / dedicated eval / private). (Samir)
- Procurement to confirm PO timing and any contract approver names. (Samir / Emily)
- I’ll share a short pricing workbook that maps commit tiers to estimated unit costs for hosted vs Dedicated. (Marissa / Ben)

Attachments: Procurement_Playbook_Olive_Custom.pdf (summary), SLA_Commit_Tiers.pdf (tiered pricing/SLA), Redwood_Pricing_Summary_v2.xlsx (workbook)

Thanks — aiming for a short call this week if you want to walk the workbook together.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olive-systems.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement readiness & hosting preference (PO vs Card)

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Pilot hosting: we prefer using the hosted API for the PoC to move quickly. Dedicated will likely be required in production if we hit latency/throughput targets, but that is Phase 2.

- Payment: procurement requires a PO for any commitment > $10k/year. For the pilot (expected <$2k/month) we can pay by card or company central card. So PO not required immediately, but we will want guidance on how the PO path looks once we decide to commit.

- Commit target: our finance lead asked whether commit tiers can be set by spend ($/month) rather than GPU hours — simpler for our accounting. Can your pricing workbook show both spend-based tiers and estimated GPU-hours equivalence?

- Security: Emily will follow up with the exact SOC2 artifact request; the attached playbook looks helpful.

We can do a short 30-min pricing alignment call on Thursday morning (May 27) if that works for you.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Khan
Director, Cloud Platform — Olive Systems
samir.khan@olive-systems.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olive-systems.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: procurement readiness & hosting preference (PO vs Card)

Samir — adding a couple of practical notes so procurement has what they need when they evaluate PO vs card and hosted vs Dedicated: 

- Billing via PO: we support Net-30 invoicing on signed contracts (standard for Dedicated & committed hosted). For pilots billed on-card, we can do monthly invoices too but those typically require a billing profile setup in our portal.

- Commit structure: we can express commits either as $/month or as committed usage (GPU-hours). For quoting, we usually present both columns; attached workbook includes a spend-first table and a GPU-hour equivalence.

- Marketplace: if you prefer buying through a cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP), that is an option for card/PO depending on the marketplace policies — note that marketplace purchases sometimes have different billing cadence and limited ability to apply custom SLA language. If procurement prefers marketplace for ease, call that out and we’ll route a marketplace quote.

- Transition plan: if pilot moves to Dedicated, we can offer a 60-day ramp credit for migration (reduces effective cost in first two months) with a signed commitment.

I’ve attached Redwood_Pricing_Summary_v2.xlsx with spend-based commit tiers and the SLA_Commit_Tiers.pdf for the ramp/credits language. Happy to walk through Thursday morning — what time suits you?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Thanks all — confirming next steps and proposing owners: 

- Samir/Emily: confirm pilot will be hosted (yes) and procurement will not request a PO for the pilot (confirmed by Samir). Please share procurement approvers if/when you expect to move to commit. (Owner: Samir)
- Ben/Kimberly: schedule a 30-min pricing alignment call Thursday 27 May at 09:00 PT (rescheduled to Friday 28 May if needed). Ben will walk through the workbook and marketplace implications. (Owner: Ben)
- Marissa: prepare a short one-page that maps purchasing paths to timelines (card pilot -> PO commit -> Dedicated/private migration) and include sample contract lead times. I’ll attach that doc to the HubSpot record. (Owner: Marissa)

Attached: Procurement_Playbook_Olive_Custom.pdf; Redwood_Pricing_Summary_v2.xlsx; SLA_Commit_Tiers.pdf

If you prefer the marketplace route later, we’ll outline tradeoffs (billing cadence, custom SLA limitations) during the call.

Best,
Marissa
